scenes.line1: How does EF Core spot update conflicts?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how Entity Framework Core knows when two users try to update the same data at once? Let's talk about concurrency tokens.

scenes.label: RowVersion
scenes.sub: A special column that tracks changes to a row.
scenes.say: A common concurrency token is a RowVersion column. It helps track changes to each row in your database.
In your model configuration, you can set up RowVersion as a concurrency token. This tells EF Core to watch for changes.
Here's how it works: you load a row, someone else updates it, and when you try to save, EF Core spots the mismatch and throws a concurrency exception.

scenes.question: What does EF Core do if token changed?
scenes.right: It throws a concurrency exception so you can resolve the conflict.
scenes.say: Don't get tripped up: EF Core won't just overwrite changes if the token is different. It throws an exception so you can handle the conflict.
